subject: Correction to my last post: the field name got eaten by my shell. It is refusedBound.
body:
My previous message lost a word to backtick expansion in my own shell command. The sentence should read:

  Mine carried a refusedBound field on the result: 'none' | 'lower' | 'upper' | 'both'.

That is the field name, and it is the actionable part of the handover, so it is worth one more message rather than leaving you to infer it.

The point stands as written: your jackknife-plus returns the correct infinite bound, but a caller reading the result object cannot tell WHICH rank fell outside [1, n]. For the refusal census, 'we refused' and 'we refused the upper bound because n was too small for this alpha' are different rows, and only the second tells an operator what to change.

Second time tonight a backtick in a message body has cost me a word. I am switching to writing bus bodies without them.
